steps.do: Sign in as admin / admin. An account holds a password only, so first create the nine people in team-roster.csv. For each one type the User ID and the Password (at least 12 characters; this lab uses lab18-demo-passphrase, which is public, so use it only on a stack nobody else can reach) and click Create account. The server must already list the roster in CALIBER_OPERATOR_USERS and CALIBER_APPROVER_USERS (see the README): those lists, not the project role, decide who may write or approve at all.
steps.see: A green note Created maya. after each, and nine rows in the table, each Active. An account an earlier cleanup disabled shows an Enable button instead.

steps.do: Sign out and sign in as maya (a team lead who holds both the operator and approver scopes). In the top bar click the + beside the workspace selector (Create workspace), name it, and click Create and select. The UI says workspace; the API says project. They are the same object.
steps.see: The workspace selector now shows the new workspace. The person who creates a workspace is its primary owner: that role cannot be removed or demoted later.

steps.do: Still as maya, open Administration and scroll to Project access. The Project for access management selector shows your workspace. For each of the other seven members in the roster type the User ID, choose the Role and click Add member. Do not add nora: she is the non-member. (The Accounts and Secrets sections show missing required scope ... caliber.admin for maya: she is an owner, not an admin, and Project access works regardless.)
steps.see: A green note Added omar to lab18-support-copilot. after each. The table lists maya (primary owner) with no Remove button and each member with the role you chose; nora is not listed.

steps.do: Sign in as victor (viewer), choose the workspace in the top bar, open Prompts, click New prompt then Write / paste, enter a Prompt name and some Prompt text, and click Create and Open. Then open Administration › Project access as victor. Sign in as priya (editor), choose the workspace, and create the prompt the same way. Still as priya, back on Prompts search for it, click Edit, change the Template, click Save new version and then Promote v2 to @prod. Finally sign in as quinn (reviewer) and try to create a prompt.
fill: Reply to the customer politely. then a blank line and Question: {question}
steps.see: For victor: project role 'viewer' cannot perform resource.write.runtime, and on Administration the line Only a project Admin can manage members. with no Add member form. For priya: the prompt opens with v1 marked Live (creating a prompt releases its first version to @prod); after the edit v2 is Live and v1 is not. For quinn: project role 'reviewer' cannot perform resource.write.runtime.
steps.asset: viewer and reviewer refused, editor creates, releases and revises a prompt

steps.where: Top bar › workspace selector (as a non-member)
steps.do: Sign in as nora, who is an operator but belongs to no workspace. Open the workspace selector.
steps.see: It holds only All workspaces: the workspace does not appear at all. Through the API every request she makes against it is a 404, not a 403: as far as she can tell it does not exist.

steps.do: As maya, open Administration › Project access and choose the workspace. Set Role for sam to Viewer, then click Remove on victor's row. Sign in as sam and try to create a prompt; check victor's workspace selector.
steps.see: A note says Changed sam to viewer., then Removed victor from the project. and his row is gone. sam is now refused (project role 'viewer' cannot perform resource.write.runtime) and victor no longer sees the workspace.

steps.do: Sign in as priya and open Settings then the API tokens tab. Name the token, keep Expires at 30 days, pick the workspace in Workspace (each is listed with your role in it), tick caliber.operator and click Create token. Copy the secret now; it is shown once.
steps.see: A green box: Copy this token now. It will not be shown again. with the calpat_... secret. Click I have copied it: the secret is gone for good. Your tokens lists support-ci as Active with its scopes and workspace. Use it as CALIBER_TOKEN with caliberctl or the SDK: it acts in this workspace, is refused (403) in any other, and can never do more than priya can.
steps.asset: token support-ci bound to the workspace

steps.do: On the support-ci row click Revoke, read the confirmation and click Revoke token.
steps.see: The row reads Revoked and its Rotate and Revoke buttons are gone. Anything still using the secret now gets 401.

steps.do: Sign in as admin and open Audit Log (only an admin can: maya sees Admin access required). Find the workspace's id first: set Actor maya and Action create_project; the row that names your workspace shows project · PRJ-... in Entity. Clear both and put that id in Entity ID, then try Action add_project_member, and finally Actor priya with Action create_personal_access_token and then revoke_personal_access_token.
steps.see: With the entity id: one create_project row by maya and seven add_project_member rows whose details name each role, one update_project_member (sam) and one remove_project_member (victor). For priya and promote_prompt: two rows, the prompt's two releases. Then for priya: a create_personal_access_token row whose details carry the workspace id and the scopes, and no secret, and later the revoke_personal_access_token row. Refused requests (a viewer's 403) write no row: the log records what changed.
steps.asset: audit rows by entity, actor and action

steps.do: Open Releases. What's live now is the live board; Timeline is the history of promotions and rollbacks. The release timeline is not workspace-scoped in the alpha, so other prompts may appear too.
steps.see: What's live now has a row for your prompt at v2 on @prod, priya as the actor; Timeline has two Promote events for it (v2, then v1), both by priya.
steps.asset: prompt release on the timeline and live board

steps.where: Any page › top bar and banner
steps.do: Look at the top bar and the banner under it. The green dot is /health (the process and the database are up); the banner is built from /readiness. You can also read both by hand: curl $CALIBER_API/health and curl $CALIBER_API/readiness.
steps.see: The amber banner says Simulated providers: eval, llm are running in fake mode and Evaluation scores are canned, not measurements.; the dot's tooltip is API and database reachable. A missing dependency would add a red Not ready line naming it, and /readiness would answer 503.
